goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:214 — A client-wide grant is ignored whenever that client already has any per-client resource, so adding an unrelated specific permission can unexpectedly revoke global admin API access to that client.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope) method at line 214, the logic is: first check if there's a resource for the specific client (line 213), and if not found, check for the 'all-clients' resource type permission (lines 215-219). However, the issue is that if a resource exists for the specific client (line 213 returns non-null), the code proceeds to evaluate permissions only on that specific resource and never checks the 'all-clients' type-level permission. This means if someone creates any permission for a specific client (even for a different scope), the existence of that client's resource will prevent the all-clients permission from being evaluated for any scope. This is a real logic bug where a client-wide grant is ignored when a per-client resource exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:78 — An all-clients view grant returns true before evaluating an explicit client-specific denial, exposing clients that the policy excludes.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel client) at line 78, the method returns true if canView() returns true (which checks for all-clients VIEW permission) before checking client-specific permissions via hasPermission(client, VIEW). This means if a user has an all-clients VIEW permission, they can view ANY client, even if there's a specific denial policy for that client. The hasPermission(client, scope) method at line 218 does check for client-specific resources first, but canView(ClientModel) short-circuits before reaching that check. This is inconsistent with the pattern shown in UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testViewUserPermissionDenyByDefault() which expects negative policies on specific resources to override positive all-resource permissions.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, there are indeed two hasPermission overloads (lines 224-248 and 250-270) plus hasGrantedPermission (lines 278-289). Both hasPermission methods contain similar scope-matching logic that iterates through permissions and checks if expectedScopes.contains(s). The hasGrantedPermission method does the same scope matching. This is a valid refactoring suggestion - the scope matching logic is duplicated across three methods. However, this is a code quality/maintainability concern rather than a bug, as the current implementation is functionally correct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:138 — getClientsWithPermission scans every client resource and runs a policy evaluation for each before returning, so large realms make each client-list request perform unbounded work and materialize every granted ID.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that getClientsWithPermission() in ClientPermissionsV2.java (lines 127-143) iterates through all resources of type CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and calls hasGrantedPermission() for each one, which performs a full policy evaluation. This is a valid performance/scalability concern for large realms. However, this is not a bug per se - the code functions correctly - but rather an architectural concern about the O(n) policy evaluations that could impact performance. The diff clearly shows this implementation pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:101 — No test grants map-roles-client-scope or verifies that it alone permits client-scope role mapping, leaving the new scope contract unprotected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` scope constant and implements `canMapClientScopeRoles()` in ClientPermissionsV2.java at line 101. Looking at the test file PermissionClientTest.java, the `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient()` test only grants `MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE` permissions but does not include `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`. There is no test that specifically verifies the `canMapClientScopeRoles()` method works correctly when only `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` is granted. This is a valid observation about missing test coverage for newly added functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:179 — Client permission tests create resources only by internal ID, so the new clientId fallback and its invalid-client failure path are unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `resolveClient` method in AdminPermissionsSchema.java (lines 175-183) that includes fallback logic: first tries `getClientById`, then falls back to `getClientByClientId`. Looking at the test file PermissionClientTest.java, the tests use `realm.admin().clients().findByClientId("myclient").get(0)` which returns a ClientRepresentation, and then pass `myclient.getId()` to createPermission. This means tests only exercise the `getClientById` path. The fallback path via `getClientByClientId` (when someone passes a clientId string instead of internal ID) is never tested, nor is the null return path when neither lookup succeeds. This is a valid observation about missing test coverage for newly added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:208 — All new authorization tests use a same-realm admin, leaving the cross-realm denial boundary untested and vulnerable to privilege regressions.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points out that the new ClientPermissionsV2 class has methods like hasPermission() that check `if (!root.isAdminSameRealm()) return false;` (lines 208, 230, 256), but the test file PermissionClientTest.java only uses `@InjectAdminClient(mode = InjectAdminClient.Mode.MANAGED_REALM, client = "myclient", user = "myadmin")` which creates same-realm admin clients. Looking at the tests, they all operate within the same realm context. The cross-realm denial path (when isAdminSameRealm() returns false) is indeed not covered by any test in this diff. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for security-sensitive authorization code.
